chapter: Billy Phillips, George Jones and the Shriners trip
title: George Jones as the rhyming bass player
summary: Jones's string band, bass tied with sash cord, and his rhymes on customers for tips.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Oh, a bass player, was it? Yeah. Yeah, I remember that. And they also used to keep all the hips or something, didn't they? You'd grab all the hips.

That string band, like he said, he had a string band, you see. He could sing, and he'd hire a good violin player, you see. And he'd hire a fella like me on a guitar, a good guitar player. And he'd take his bass while, he wasn't, he was no kind of bass player, he just tuned, half of the time he wasn't even tuned up. Just any kind of way you know.
I think Johnny St. Cyr said he used to use ropes.

Yeah, he used to take, uh, he'd break a string, you know, one of his, uh, string. He'd get an old sash cord and put it on there. And they could rouse him, and rouse him up and put it on there and wind up, go on, let's go. And, you don't tell him you ain't tuned, just let him go, but he's a money getter though. Yeah. Yeah, you see, he could take and, uh, see you'd have a bunch of men, and, uh, he was well-liked. And he'd get a, he could rhyme. See, like you named Mr. Russell, somebody, meet him in the back and tell him that man in there, the name is Mr. Russell. He's in the shoe business, or he's in such and such a business. And he'd come on in and start to sing and play and rhyme on you, and make all kind of rhymes on you. Then, then you would know how you got your name, you see. Johnny St. Cyr, talking about the same thing. Somebody in the gang had done told him, you know, that your name. Well, quite naturally, after he rhymed so good on you, you'd get your wallet off when you get through it and give him a $5, $10 bill, something like that. Well, he was good. But, before I was playing the bass, he couldn't, he had an old rag cracked up bass. He didn't care to throw it around any kind of way. And I went all the way to Indianapolis, Indiana with him.
